name: bonding_bond_create_8d6184e4881b
bug: A real bug that shipped in Linux until 2010: when register_netdevice() fails, bond_create() returns without free_netdev(), leaking the net_device allocated by alloc_netdev_mq(). Upstream commit 8d6184e4881b added the release; removing it from Linux 6.18.55 restores the original bug.
reachable: bonding_init() calls bond_create() for each of max_bonds (default 1) at module load and propagates its error, so failing an allocation inside register_netdevice() with fail-nth makes initialisation fail and leaves the net_device unreferenced.

history.subject: bonding: fix device leak on error in bond_create()

evidence.reason: leak at bond_main.c:6497 after failing bond_create+0x66/0xa0

name: null_blk_alloc_dev
bug: null_alloc_dev() allocates the struct nullb_device with kzalloc() and frees it with kfree(dev) when badblocks_init() fails. Removing that call leaks the nullb_device: dev is a local variable that has not been published anywhere yet, and NULL is returned.
reachable: null_init() calls null_alloc_dev() at module load; when it returns NULL, init fails with -ENOMEM and the module is unloaded, so failing the allocation inside badblocks_init() with fail-nth leaves the object unreferenced.

evidence.reason: leak at main.c:799 after failing null_alloc_dev+0x63/0x210
